text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Centre Party said yes and the Development Party said no to Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi's offer to help him rebuild his government coalition.
- The three Baltic presidents reiterated in Riga their countries' wish to be among the first members of NATO.
- The foreign ministers of Estonia and Slovenia signed a free trade deal.
- Baltic defence cooperation could be developed if there was the political will to set aside the money, the commanders of the Baltic states' armed forces said.
- Tiit Made, a leading member of the Development Party, said they would not enter a government with the Centre Party even if they were offered to the post of U.N. Secretary-General.
- A second group of Estonian peacekeepers is to leave today for a mission in south Lebanon to serve under Norwegian leadership.
- The stock exchange had a record day, led by record trade in Hansapank.
